bank.q: My parents ___ at home now.
bank.why: Parents jamak, jadi are.

bank.q: The shop ___ at nine every morning.
bank.why: Subjek tunggal (the shop) di present simple: verb + s, jadi opens.

bank.q: We ___ a movie last night.
bank.why: Last night menandakan masa lalu: watched.

bank.q: The cat is sleeping ___ the sofa.
bank.why: On the sofa = di atas sofa.

bank.q: It is very ___ today. Take your umbrella.
bank.why: Karena disuruh membawa payung, cuacanya rainy (hujan).

bank.q: We see with our ___.
bank.why: Eyes = mata, alat untuk melihat.

bank.q: This is my sister's room. It is ___ room.
bank.why: Sister perempuan tunggal, jadi her.

bank.q: ___ you like tea? No, I prefer coffee.
bank.why: Pertanyaan present simple dengan I/you/we/they memakai Do.

bank.q: ___ late for school, please.
bank.why: Larangan: Don't + verb dasar. Don't be late = jangan terlambat.

bank.q: There are sixty minutes in one ___.
bank.why: Satu hour (jam) = 60 menit.

bank.q: I ___ him yesterday at the station.
bank.why: Yesterday menandakan waktu lampau yang jelas: past simple (saw).

bank.q: She has never ___ sushi before.
bank.why: Has/have + past participle: has never eaten.

bank.q: I have no plans for tonight. Maybe I ___ my friend.
bank.why: Keputusan spontan/kemungkinan saat berbicara memakai will + verb (maybe).

bank.q: If you mix red and yellow, you ___ orange.
bank.why: Fakta umum: If + present simple, present simple (get).

bank.q: She said, "I am tired." -> She said that she ___ tired.
bank.why: Dalam reported speech tense mundur: am menjadi was.

bank.q: My new job is ___ than my old one.
bank.why: Adjective panjang: more + adjective + than.

bank.q: I decided ___ a new phone.
bank.why: Setelah decide dipakai to + verb.

bank.q: Can you ___ after my cat while I am away?
bank.why: Look after = merawat/menjaga.

bank.q: We need to ___ in at the airport two hours before the flight.
bank.why: Check in = lapor/daftar masuk di bandara.

bank.q: This is the restaurant ___ we had dinner last week.
bank.why: Where dipakai untuk tempat.

bank.q: If he ___ harder, he would have passed the exam.
bank.why: Third conditional: If + past perfect, would have + past participle.

bank.q: It is raining cats and dogs, so we cannot go out. This idiom means it is raining ___.
bank.why: Raining cats and dogs = hujan sangat deras.

bank.q: She told me she ___ the report before the meeting.
bank.why: Kejadian yang selesai lebih dulu dari kejadian lampau lain: past perfect.

bank.q: He asked me ___ I could help him.
bank.why: Pertanyaan ya/tidak dalam reported speech memakai if atau whether.

bank.q: We stayed at home ___ the weather was terrible.
bank.why: Because = karena, menyatakan sebab.

bank.q: You will not pass ___ you study harder.
bank.why: Unless = kecuali jika. Maksudnya: tidak akan lulus kecuali belajar lebih giat.

bank.q: The lights are off. They ___ be at home.
bank.why: Can't be = pasti tidak. Lampu mati, jadi mereka pasti tidak di rumah.

bank.q: I wish I ___ taller. Then I could play basketball.
bank.why: Wish untuk keadaan tidak nyata sekarang: past simple (were).

bank.q: She always ___ attention to small details.
bank.why: Kolokasi tetap: pay attention.

bank.q: He is very good ___ solving problems.
bank.why: Kolokasi tetap: good at.

bank.q: I will not go to the party ___ I am invited.
bank.why: Unless = kecuali, sama dengan if ... not.

bank.q: Anna loves running, ___ her brother hates any kind of exercise.
bank.why: Whereas menyatakan kontras antara dua orang.

bank.q: If I ___ you, I would accept the offer.
bank.why: Dalam kondisi tidak nyata, were dipakai untuk semua subjek: If I were you.

bank.q: Under no circumstances ___ the door be left open.
bank.why: Negatif di awal kalimat: should + subjek dibalik. Under no circumstances should the door ...

bank.q: ___ from the top of the hill, the village looks tiny.
bank.why: Desa dilihat (pasif), jadi past participle: Seen from the top ...

bank.q: The new law will ___ the economy, so prices are expected to rise.
bank.why: Affect = memengaruhi (kata kerja). Effect biasanya kata benda.

bank.q: The two companies decided to ___ forces to launch the product.
bank.why: Kolokasi tetap: join forces = bergabung/bekerja sama.

bank.q: It was in 1998 ___ the company was founded.
bank.why: Cleft sentence: It was + keterangan + that + klausa.

bank.q: There ___ be a cinema here, but now it is a supermarket.
bank.why: Used to + verb dasar = dulu pernah (sekarang tidak lagi).

bank.q: He spilled the beans about the surprise party. He ___ the secret.
bank.why: Spill the beans = membocorkan rahasia.

articles.title: The Night Market
body: Every Friday evening, there is a night market near our town. It opens at six and closes at eleven. Many families go there after work.
There are small stalls with food, clothes and toys. My favorite is the fried noodle stall. The cook is very fast, and the noodles are always hot and delicious.
Last Friday, I went with my cousin. We ate noodles, drank iced tea and bought a small bag. We got home at ten, tired but happy.

qs.q: When does the night market open?
What is the writer's favorite stall?
Who went to the market with the writer last Friday?

articles.title: The Value of a Second Language
body: Learning a second language is often seen as a useful skill for travel or work, but its benefits go further. Research suggests that bilingual people are better at switching between tasks and ignoring distractions.
Language learning may also protect the brain as we age. Some studies have found that bilingual people develop signs of memory loss several years later than those who speak only one language.

Of course, becoming fluent takes time and regular practice. Experts recommend studying a little every day instead of cramming once a week, because frequent short sessions help the brain remember new words.

qs.q: According to research, bilingual people are better at
opts: switching between tasks and ignoring distractions

qs.q: What have some studies found about bilingual people?
opts: Signs of memory loss appear later in life
